LESSON: READING 11.2.1 FLUENCY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Community Leaders Suggested vocabulary Chief, leader, group leader, head teacher
Topic 11.2: Reading 11.2.1 Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 11.2.1 Fluency, part of Community Leaders Suggested vocabulary Chief, leader, group leader, head teacher in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why is proper articulation of sounds important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 11.2.1 Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration – learner’s speaking skills are enhanced as they take part in timed-reading competitions collaboratively.

Values:
Respect: the learner understands and appreciates others during reading competitions.

88

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
• Citizenship (social cohesion) - Learners work collaboratively while taking part in timed-reading competitions.

• Learner support programmes (clubs and society) - Learners recite poems in reading clubs.

Link to other learning areas

The learner’s capacity to read and understand concepts in other learning areas is greatly improved as they become more fluent in reading.

Suggested learning resources

• Textbooks in print and in braille

• Audio recording

• Digital devices with assistive technology

• Learners are guided to listen to short

audio clips of paragraphs containing

words with the target sounds: / ʃ/, /tʃ/

/θ/, /ð/.

• Learners are guided to read words

with the target sounds adhering to the

correct pronunciation.

• Learner with low vision to watch

while learners with blindness to listen

to audio-visual clip on reading target

sounds fluently.

• Learners are guided to individually,

read simple sentences in the story

aloud paying attention to the

punctuation.

• Learners take part in timed-reading

competitions.

• Learners are guided to recite poems/

rhymes related to the theme.
